html:
Zoe Porphyrogenita was a Byzantine empress of the Macedonian dynasty, a niece of Basil II, who made three men emperor and briefly ruled in her own right in 1042. Her name means "born in the purple", that is, to a reigning emperor.

As the old emperor's daughter she was the key to the throne. She was married only in 1028, at about fifty, to Romanos III, on her dying father Constantine VIII's orders. After Romanos drowned in his bath in 1034, perhaps murdered, she married her young lover, who became Michael IV. His nephew Michael V, whom she adopted, then tried to get rid of her and sent her to a convent in 1042.

The people of Constantinople rose in fury to restore their rightful empress, and Michael V was blinded. Zoe ruled with her sister Theodora for two months, then married a third time, to Constantine IX Monomachos. The courtier Michael Psellos knew her and describes her vividly. Her portrait, beside Constantine IX, is still in a mosaic in Hagia Sophia.
